definition: Ballad means a slow, sentimental song that tells a story, often of love.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word ballad. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know ballad should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Halfway through the set, the fiddler traded her reels for a ballad about a soldier writing home from the border.
A jingle is far lighter than a ballad — thirty catchy seconds built to sell something, while a ballad carries characters and their story through verse after verse.
A lament goes further than a ballad — the ballad's story gives way entirely to grieving, sung sorrow with no plot left.

A folk song is any traditional song passed along by ordinary singers — work songs, dance tunes, love songs alike. A ballad is the storytelling branch of that family: slow, sentimental, built around characters and a plot. Every ballad could live as a folk song, but most folk songs tell no story.

A serenade is sung to one particular listener, usually to court or honor them — the audience is the point. A ballad is sung for anyone who will listen and carries a story with characters and feeling. The serenade's job is the wooing; the ballad's job is the tale.

Every December, the Cooper's Hollow miners' choir closes its concert with the same slow number, and nobody in the valley needs the program to name it.
Written after the 1907 flood at the No.
4 shaft, the ballad follows one lamp boy from his kitchen goodbye, down the lift, through the rescue, and home again — a verse for each chapter, eleven verses in all.
It is not a quick or clever piece.
What holds the hall is the story: listeners who have heard it fifty times still lean forward for the verse where the rope holds.
Newcomers sometimes ask why the choir doesn't trim it to three minutes.
The director always gives the same answer: cut a verse and you cut a chapter.
The song has outlived the mine, the company, and the railroad that served them.
The boy's name is on no monument, but every winter the valley sings him home.
